owner_creation.analysis: The insert_mode private lbool owns insert-versus-overwrite policy, initially insert; an editor action toggles it and cmd_istr temporarily forces insertion.
owner_creation.invariant: Editing policy is separate from owned command bytes.
limitations: insert_mode is editing policy, not ownership of inserted bytes.

aliases_escapes.analysis: cmd_istr saves a copied Boolean while borrowing source text; no pointer into that source is stored in the insert_mode policy field.
aliases_escapes.invariant: Saved mode state cannot keep source text live.
limitations: Temporary overrides must not be observed by another editor operation.

callback_targets.analysis: cmd_ichar may directly delete a character before insertion in overwrite mode; the insert_mode flag contains no dynamic edit callback or closure.
callback_targets.invariant: Overwrite behavior is a direct policy branch.
limitations: The cited termination handler does not by itself prove an insert_mode reentry route.

invalidation.analysis: cmd_istr restores insert_mode on normal return, but no RAII guard restores its temporary override on every nonlocal/fatal path.
invalidation.invariant: Temporary mode lifetime depends on normal function return.
limitations: The scoped concern is another editor observing a temporary insert_mode override; no exclusive owner currently excludes that reentry.

mutation_commit.analysis: insert_mode selects deletion before overwrite insertion; that choice does not preserve self-aliasing source bytes or make replacement failure-atomic.
mutation_commit.invariant: Mode choice does not commit a complete byte replacement.

release_pair.analysis: The insert_mode bit has no allocator release pair; restoring its old value neither restores deleted text nor retires any completion/history allocation.
release_pair.invariant: Policy rollback is distinct from storage rollback.
limitations: Restoring insert_mode does not restore a moved or invalidated command cursor.

error_cleanup.analysis: cmd_istr restores the insert_mode saved mode after an action error breaks its loop; fatal/reentrant paths still lack an exclusive editor transaction.
error_cleanup.invariant: Ordinary action errors and fatal cleanup have different paths.

signals_handoff.analysis: insert_mode is temporarily overridden by ordinary editor operations. A second editor observing the override would use the wrong policy, but the terminate -> quit citation does not establish that such an operation is reachable from a handler. No concrete asynchronous insert_mode mutation is claimed; exclusive editor entry remains a required precondition.
signals_handoff.invariant: Insert-mode review does not approve asynchronous editing.
limitations: Source-specific review of coupled legacy editor state; M0-MEM-001 remains open and no new runtime defect is asserted from raw-pointer structure alone.

src/signal.rs.relationship: src/signal.rs:83-85 reaches quit but does not invoke an editor or alter insert_mode. Observing a temporary insert override from a handler is a conditional editor-entry concern, not an established path.
